top_story.headline: Education Department orders a $237,405 print-fleet transition from AlphaSix without competition, saying its old contract ended one day before the new one had to start
top_story.dek: The justification was posted October 23, more than three weeks after the October 1 start date it gives for the order.
paragraphs: The Education Department's Federal Student Aid office posted a justification on October 23 for a sole-source delivery order to AlphaSix for managed print services. The order runs through the NASA SEWP V contract vehicle (contract number NNG15SD28B) and covers networked multifunction devices, installation, maintenance, supplies, secure print functions and transition support. The estimated value in the description of the action is $237,405.22, although the form's header lists $209,360.64. The base year is October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2027, with one option year. The agency cites urgent need under the exception to fair opportunity, meaning it skipped the competition among existing contract holders.

The document says the office's current devices come off the department-wide contract effective September 30, 2026, and the new order must be effective by October 1. It says this leaves no gap in which to remove, replace and configure a different fleet. It also says the timing is "substantially shorter than the transition period contemplated by the Performance Work Statement, which allows up to 60 calendar days for transition-in," and calls it "an unforeseen shift." The document adds that the existing fleet is tied to HP lease and service agreements "held through the current contractor," and that the order is meant to keep printing running "while the Government completes a competitive follow-on acquisition." It does not name the current contractor.

sections.headline: Indian Health Service plans to sole-source immunization training to Johns Hopkins University, which built the program being adapted
paragraphs: 13 new sole-source justifications, 9 of them posted under other notice types (Special Notices and Award Notices), and 12 repeats from earlier editions left out. The Education Department print order is today's Top Story. The two cards below are the items with the clearest stories, and nothing else stands out as unusual.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: Indian Health Service plans to give Johns Hopkins University a sole-source contract to adapt the immunization training the university built
meta: only one company can do it
Department of Health and Human Services, Indian Health Service
blocks.text: The notice of intent, posted as a Special Notice, covers a 12-month contract for peer-to-peer immunization training and curriculum deployment for providers serving American Indian and Alaska Native communities. The agency says it will tailor an existing training program "previously developed by the intended source." Johns Hopkins is an academic institution rather than a typical contractor, and USAspending shows federal contracts under its name going back to 1997. No justification document was attached, so only the notice text was read and no value is given.

blocks.title: Veterans Affairs plans to upgrade the Washington, D.C., VA Medical Center's pneumatic tube controls with the system's maker, TransLogic, without competition
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The notice was posted as a Special Notice for the medical center at 50 Irving Street NW. The statement of work says the tube system's controls are end-of-life, that "replacement parts are no longer available," and that the manufacturer is sunsetting the Nexus software. It says TransLogic Corporation "is the OEM of this system and the sole qualified source for the Version 8 migration." The work covers 16 stations, 12 transfer units and 2 blowers. It includes a new air-gap network, 16 battery backup retrofit kits and replacement of 14 control boards.
Also worth a look

items: Veterans Affairs gives the Agile 4 Vets joint venture a $683,093 task order for 30 days of External Provider Scheduling pilot support without competition. The joint venture comprises HRS Consulting, Oxford Government Consulting and 4th Sector, and the order covers support and training for the pilot and its Wave 0 expansion. (JEFO-36C10X25D0017_36C10X26N0172)

Veterans Affairs buys $35,945 of advanced red-cell blood testing from Versiti Blood Health without competition. The justification says most commercial reference labs outsource complex gel-method antibody identification to Versiti, and that labs such as Quest Diagnostics and LabCorp can do only part of the menu. It was posted as an Award Notice. (36C25627Q0016)

Navy plans to buy mast weldment and tube assemblies for its Ship Signal Exploitation Equipment from Concurrent Technologies Corporation without competition. The notice of intent covers parts for the Increment F system, and no value is given. (N66001-27-Q-6003)
Environmental Protection Agency's Region 3 office renews Apex Instruments air-monitoring equipment and proprietary consumables for $41,000 on a brand-name-only basis. (Apex Instruments notice)

sections.headline: Social Security Administration extends its Richmond, Indiana, lease without competition a day before it expires
paragraphs: Three new extensions or bridges: two Social Security Administration lease extensions handled by the General Services Administration and a bridge contract for Noblis at the Defense Threat Reduction Agency.

blocks.title: General Services Administration extends the Social Security Administration's Richmond, Indiana, lease for 60 months without competition, a day before it expires
meta: Landlord/Lessor, 500 N A St, Richmond, IN
only one company can do it
General Services Administration, Public Buildings Service
blocks.text: The memo to file says lease LIN16319 "will expire on October 24, 2026," and it was posted October 23. The agency's stated reason is that Social Security Administration locations "require security upgrades in all their locations and the current location cannot accommodate these." It says the extension gives the agency time "to come up with their new requirements, which are not finished yet." The annual rent is redacted but described as within the simplified lease acquisition threshold. The memo is signed by Lease Contracting Officer Joel Wilson.

blocks.title: General Services Administration extends the Social Security Administration's Manteca, California, lease for 60 months without competition, posted after the lease's stated expiration
meta: only one company can do it
General Services Administration, Public Buildings Service
blocks.text: The justification covers 8,610 usable square feet (8,959 rentable) under lease LCA02551, which it says expires October 11, 2026. The extension would start October 12, 2026. The notice was posted October 23. The agency says the Social Security Administration "encountered delays in establishing its long-term requirements for this facility," and that the extra term lets it "right-size its space utilization." The rent and total value are redacted.

items: Defense Threat Reduction Agency plans a bridge sole-source contract for Noblis advisory and assistance services on its Cooperative Threat Reduction Program. It runs one year with two six-month options, and the notice cites a statutory authority. The pipeline has logged an earlier Noblis sole-source justification for Department of Homeland Security advisory services. (Notice, earlier Noblis justification)

sections.headline: Army Corps of Engineers' West Haven VA hospital job pairs brand-name justifications for Johnson Controls with a question disputing one of them
paragraphs: 111 new solicitations, with 45 repeats left out. Ten of the 13 flagged notices were repeats of earlier listings with only deadline or amendment changes, so they are left out. The items below include documents read today on notices posted earlier.

blocks.title: Army Corps of Engineers' VA West Haven chilled-water job carries Johnson Controls sole-source justifications and a question saying one misstates the company's campus work
meta: Department of the Army, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers New England District
blocks.text: These documents were read today on a notice posted earlier. The solicitation is W912WJ26RA008 for a chilled water plant and site utilities at the West Haven VA Medical Center. One justification posted August 24 says the campus's building automation is "standardized on two original equipment manufacturer platforms including Johnson Controls, Inc. (JCI), which is the predominant platform deployed across the campus, and Siemens." Another says Johnson Controls' access control and cameras rely on "proprietary field controllers and a proprietary controller-to-host communication architecture." A third file is named for Johnson Controls fire alarms. Amendment 0003 (October 6) carries a ProjNet inquiry flagging "an error in the document," saying the statement that Johnson Controls does not work on construction projects for the campus "is also inaccurate." The same amendment's specifications say the video surveillance system "should have facial recognition software to assist in identifying individuals for current and future purposes."

blocks.title: Navy issues a request for proposals to dismantle and dispose of the ex-USS Long Beach, a decommissioned nuclear-powered cruiser
meta: Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command
blocks.text: The notice calls for proposals to transport, dismantle, de-militarize and dispose of ex-Long Beach (CGN9), "including the defueled reactor plants." It is tied to an earlier request for information that included industry day, tour and data library instructions. An earlier edition listed this solicitation on October 7.

sections.headline: Secret Service's recruiting Q&A confirms a surge-hiring push toward about 4,000 hires through 2028
paragraphs: 71 new combined synopsis/solicitations, with 37 repeats left out. The lead item comes from a document read today on a notice posted earlier.

blocks.title: Secret Service says it is in a surge-hiring environment and confirms a goal of about 4,000 hires through 2028
meta: Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Secret Service
blocks.text: This comes from a Q&A spreadsheet posted May 1, 2026 on solicitation 70US0926R70093666 for national recruitment advertising, read today. The agency says it is "operating in a surge hiring environment" for Special Agent and Secret Service Police roles. It confirmed that "approximately 4,000 hires through 2028 is directionally accurate as a cumulative, multi-year workforce expansion goal." The goal is "approximately 70,000+ applicants annually." Because Secret Service Police must be based in the Washington, D.C., area, it "places a heightened emphasis on strategies that directly support D.C. focused recruiting."

items: Army contracting office solicits three services for Angkor Sentinel 27: base life support facility rehabilitation, catering and transportation. Quotes are due November 20, 2026. (base life support, catering, transportation)

sections.headline: Immigration and Customs Enforcement adds $44.8 million to Ardent Group's pharmacy benefit contract for its Health Service Corps
paragraphs: 8 new awards of $2 million or more (none from the Defense Department backlog), 3 large modifications and 1 cut. 4 are written up here, and the 8 routine ones are listed, each linked, in "USAspending: Every Other New Award" at the end of the edition.

blocks.text: Ardent Group, LLC received a $44,769,832 modification (P00006) from the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement on October 22, exercising Option Period 1 of its contract. The contract provides the agency's Health Service Corps with a pharmacy benefit manager to handle the drug formulary, claims processing, pharmacy network administration and benefit plan design. Award.

Accenture Federal Services LLC received a $150,807,170 modification (P00004) from the Department of Veterans Affairs on October 22. It is described as a funding-only action for option year 1: incremental funding and a ceiling reallocation on the electronic health record modernization system integration contract. The description cites Executive Order 14398. Award.

Vivsoft Technologies LLC won a $10,473,395 award signed October 20 from the General Services Administration's Federal Acquisition Service, described as "Operational Enterprise Services OES III" for engineering and technical support, classified under computer systems design services. The description does not say which agency the work serves. Award.

Battle's Transportation, Inc. received a $2,715,912 task order from the Department of Veterans Affairs, signed October 22, for wheelchair van transportation at the Washington, D.C., VA Medical Center. Award.
Other notable awards

footer.coverage_window: October 23-24, 2026 (Pacific time), with a trailing sweep for USAspending contract actions plus the Defense Department's 90-day-delayed releases.
footer.sources: OMB apportionment data via openomb.org and apportionment-public.max.gov; USAspending.gov API; SAM.gov contract opportunities and their attached documents.
footer.known_gaps: No source errors were reported. OMB apportionments: no new apportionment files were approved in the five-day window. SAM.gov documents: 1,005 attachments on 192 notices were queued, 168 were screened this run, and 35 failed to read. Of the files not read, 642 are queued for a later edition and 48 are access-restricted on SAM.gov, and 4,024 files in total are queued for later editions. Roughly 406 links to outside portals (DIBBS, NECO, PIEE and others) were not followed. The Johns Hopkins, Noblis, Concurrent Technologies and Apex Instruments justifications were judged from the notice text, with no full justification document read for the first three.
